newsitem.title: GERMANY: Kok says EMU criteria, timetable must be adhered to.
newsitem.headline: Kok says EMU criteria, timetable must be adhered to.

text.p: Dutch Prime Minister Wim Kok said on Monday that the timetable and entry criteria for the start of European monetary union must be adhered to.

Kok, speaking at a ceremony to hand over the presidency of the European Monetary Institute, forerunner to the planned European Central Bank, said countries must also make more efforts to fulfil criteria laid out in the Maastricht Treaty.
"We have to keep on doing what it takes to bring about a
strong, unified currency," Kok said in the text of a speech.
"We have to stick to the timetable and the convergence rules as set out in the Maastricht Treaty," Kok said. "It would be politically and economically unwise to depart from the original plans."
Kok also said European nations must ensure that a prudent financial discipline policy is maintained after the start of the new currency in January 1999.
"The participants must be in good condition both at the start and during the race," Kok said.
Kok said it was "absolutely essential" to keep the process toward the start of EMU on track.
"Hesitation now would harm the Union's cogency and credibility. Tremendous efforts have been and are being made. There is a great deal at stake. We really cannot afford to let EMU fail," Kok said.
